summary: Georgia tower list places Woodcliff in Screven County at elevation 300 (no unit stated; read as feet); its gfc-108 tag is an older Forestry Commission list number, not a lookout register number.

evidence.supports: Woodcliff is listed at 32.72902, -81.74300 in Screven County, elevation 300, with tag gfc-108
The gfc-nnn numbers come from an older GFC list of 203 towers
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn)

evidence.supports: The National Historic Lookout Register lists 29 registered Georgia towers
evidence.quote: There are 29 lookouts registered in Georgia.

evidence.supports: Aircraft patrols have largely replaced tower operators
evidence.quote: Patrols using planes like this one have largely replaced fire tower operators

evidence.supports: Georgia has steadily cut tower staffing since the late 1980s
evidence.quote: Since the late 1980s, the state has steadily cut its fire tower staff

evidence.supports: 137 of 144 surviving towers were no longer staffed
evidence.quote: 137 of the state's 144 still-existing towers are no longer staffed

evidence.supports: The 137 of 144 figures come from a Forestry Commission spreadsheet
evidence.quote: The real numbers are revealed in a forestry commission spreadsheet generated earlier this year

evidence.supports: The state was auctioning towers off
evidence.quote: The towers are being auctioned off

evidence.supports: Some towers were sold for scrap or to hunting clubs
evidence.quote: sold for scrap metal in some cases, or to hunting clubs or other groups

evidence.supports: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register lists two Georgia sites
evidence.quote: There are 2 former lookout sites registered in Georgia.

sources.title: Fire towers are fading into history
sources.publisher: Savannah Morning News (Savannah Now), archived copy

corrections.proposed: Remove. 108 is a number from an older Georgia Forestry Commission list (gfc-108 on the tnlandforms list), not a lookout register number.
corrections.why: The NHLR Georgia list has 29 towers and does not include Woodcliff. The tnlandforms legend says gfc-nnn numbers come from an older GFC list, and the entry reads gfc-108.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The GFC US 108 register entry in the record is not supported by any source read; a correction is proposed. The tnlandforms entry also carries a code 'stoop-to' that I could not interpret and did not use. Elevation unit read as feet (the record's 91.4 m equals 300 ft); the list does not state its unit. No build date, status, staffing or access data was found. Paragraphs 3 and 4 are statewide and register context, not facts about this tower; drop them if the story is held. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the NHLR and Former Fire Lookout Sites Georgia lists were read in full, and neither includes this tower. The story now says the tnlandforms list gives no elevation unit. The proposed removal of GFC US 108 in corrections is not applied here, because the tower record is outside this check's scope. Web searches used: 2.
